sources.entry: pydantic-monty - A secure Python sandbox written in Rust for running AI-written code.

summary.one_liner: Monty is a secure Python sandbox written in Rust for safely running AI/LLM-generated code without a container-based sandbox.
summary.what_it_does: Monty is a Python sandbox written in Rust, intended for running code that an AI model has written. It is installed as a package (pydantic-monty for Python, @pydantic/monty for JavaScript/TypeScript, and the monty crate for Rust). Inside the sandbox there is no filesystem, environment variables, or network; the code can reach the host only through functions and mounts the caller passes in. The Python usage example shows a pool of sandboxes with sessions, where host-side external functions are called from the sandboxed code and inputs are passed in. The README claims a new sandbox starts in under 1ms from a warm pool. A separate commercial option runs the same sandbox as a gRPC-streamed service in a container image. The README also mentions docs covering the security model, resource limits, snapshots, and the supported Python subset.
use_cases: give sandboxed code controlled access to host functions
embed a restricted Python interpreter in an application
notable: No filesystem, environment variables, or network access inside the sandbox; host access only through passed-in functions and mounts
Claimed sandbox startup under 1ms from a running pool, versus about 1500ms for a sandbox service
Snapshots, resource limits, and a documented Python subset
Used for Code Mode in Pydantic AI; community bindings for Go and Dart/Flutter
caveats: Commercial Support (gRPC server, container image) is a paid offering separate from the MIT-licensed OSS package
Runs a Python 3.14 subset rather than full CPython, per the documentation references
Latency figures are the project's own claims in the README
